name: Battery Health
author: Manuel Vázquez Acosta
description: Long-term battery health history: capacity retention and charge cycles tracked at the moment they change, plus a recent charge-level graph. Polls adaptively and reacts to charge-state changes.

barWidget.description: Capacity retention (charge_full / charge_full_design) tracked over time, with wear rate, cycle count, an end-of-life projection and a recent charge-level graph. Samples every 10 minutes while current is flowing and backs off when idle.

schema.label: Polling interval while charging or discharging (seconds)
schema.description: How often sysfs is read while current is flowing. This is the cadence that shapes the charge graph.

schema.label: Polling interval while idle (seconds)
schema.description: How often sysfs is read while the battery is neither charging nor draining. Nothing moves in this state, so polling backs off.

schema.label: Charge graph window (days)
schema.description: How far back the charge and power graph reaches, and how long those samples are kept. The graph narrows to the data it actually has, so a fresh install still fills the frame.

schema.label: Health history retention (days)
schema.description: How far back health samples are kept. A sample is stored only when the capacity or cycle count moves, plus a heartbeat every six hours, so even the maximum stays a small file.

schema.label: Bar readout
schema.description: What the bar widget shows: the live charge level, the capacity retention, or the cycle count. Text only — omarchy.power already carries a battery glyph, and this widget usually sits next to it.

schema.label: Battery name
schema.description: Optional. A specific /sys/class/power_supply entry such as BAT0 or BAT1. Empty means the first battery that reports a design capacity.
